papers.title: Mi-Ripple: Restoring Images Degraded by Iterative AI Editing
papers.desc: Iterative reference-conditioned image editing can introduce grid-like and granular textures, commonly described as digital ripple.

papers.title: Memory as Plans: World-Action Modeling with Memory-Grounded Planning
papers.desc: Mainstream robotic policies often adopt a Markovian formulation, but many complex real-world manipulation tasks are inherently non-Markovian, requiring long-horizon memory beyond the current observation.

papers.title: FreeFlow: A Bias-free Hierarchical Transformer for Optical Flow Estimation
papers.desc: Optical flow methods typically rely on task-specific inductive biases, such as correlation volumes, feature warping, and iterative refinement, among others, to reach high accuracy.

papers.title: Studying Image Tokenizers as Visual Languages in Unified Multimodal Models
papers.desc: Image tokenizers define the ``visual language'' of unified multimodal models, yet are commonly studied through isolated metrics or generation-/understanding-only evaluations.

papers.title: MetroLLM-Bench: Evaluating Language Models as Transit Kiosk Runtimes
papers.desc: We introduce MetroLLM-Bench, a 955-case benchmark for testing language models as the policy layer of a transit kiosk.

papers.title: TempCloze: Can Video-LLMs Identify the Missing Middle?
papers.desc: Temporal reasoning benchmarks for Video-LLMs are often mediated by language, leaving room for linguistic shortcuts from option wording, answer correlations, or language priors.

papers.title: Negative Self-Distillation: Learning to Reason by Avoiding Flaws
papers.desc: On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) has emerged as a popular paradigm for large language model (LLM) self-improvement, allowing models to act as their own teachers by leveraging privileged information such as ground-truth solutions.

papers.title: UniH^3: Unifying Hierarchical Homogeneity and Heterogeneity for All-in-One Medical Image Restoration
papers.desc: All-in-One medical image restoration (MedIR) aims to address diverse tasks across modalities and degradation types using a single universal model.

papers.title: Building Multilingual Bridges: Data Mixing as the Pillar of Generalization for In-Language Reasoning
papers.desc: Reasoning language models have made substantial advances on a variety of complex tasks, yet their capabilities remain overwhelmingly English-centric: models primarily reason in English regardless of the language they are prompted in.

papers.title: Think Before You Link: Rarity, Reasoning, and Retrieval in Multilingual Entity Linking
papers.desc: Multimodal entity linking grounds entity mentions in text and images to knowledge-base entries.

papers.title: Adaptive Bridge: A Proxy-Based Decoupling Layer for Mitigating DDS Backpressure in ROS 2
papers.desc: In systems built on Robot Operating System 2 (ROS 2) and using Data Distribution Service (DDS), a single network-impaired or throttled subscriber on a RELIABLE topic can cause backpressure that degrades throughput and latency for all other subscribers, including safety-critical ones sharing the publisher, because the publisher's DDS writer can no longer accept new samples.

papers.title: Beyond Solver Verdicts: Generative Reward Models for Autoformalization
papers.desc: Neurosymbolic systems rely on mathematical solvers to guarantee reasoning correctness, yet solvers are fundamentally blind to whether a formal translation maintains strict reference-equivalence to a designated formalization.

papers.title: DRG-MAPPO: Hierarchical Dynamic Role-Graph Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Cooperative Air Combat
papers.desc: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) has emerged as a pivotal paradigm for complex decision-making in autonomous systems and air combat.

papers.title: ActReview: Rebuttal-Guided Training Data and Rubric Rewards for Actionable Peer Review Generation
papers.desc: As LLMs are increasingly used for pre-submission self-review, there is growing demand for feedback that not only identifies weaknesses but also guides authors toward concrete revisions.

papers.title: IdeaAMBIG: Benchmarking Implementation-Critical Gaps in Research-Idea Specifications
papers.desc: A research idea may be novel, coherent, and scientifically plausible, yet its proposed method may remain insufficiently specified for faithful implementation.
